title: Merrily We Go

beats.what: Fatima and Elgin negotiate shared culpability in private; both acknowledge they will never be the same
At Jim's burial, Boyd's eulogy breaks down; he cannot find words
Ethan asks Victor about lakes; Victor refuses but is bargained into leading Ethan to the Brundles
Boyd offers suicidal Acosta a reason to live: investigate the storage shed as a detective would
Julie and Randall enter the collapsed house to retrieve the children's books for Storywalking research
Ethan learns from Victor about the Lake of Tears; Jade joins the search

character_beats.beat: Wants to unlock the memories that will explain why they are trapped, but cannot stop pushing even when warned the knowledge costs lives
Wants to give Acosta a reason to survive but the reason he offers (investigate the dead) is a mirror of his own inability to grieve or stop
Wants to find proof that Jim's ghost was real by locating the Lake of Tears; treats discovery as a way to un-lose his father

key_lines.line: This place took advantage of both of us. Neither of us will ever be the same again.
key_lines.why: Fatima names the shared contamination without assigning blame, enabling the episode's theme of collective grief

key_lines.line: Before we got here, I thought monsters were made up, too.
key_lines.why: Ethan's rebuttal to Jade's skepticism; collapses the line between children's fiction and lived reality

key_lines.line: You remind me of someone I could have helped and I didn't.
key_lines.why: Boyd's admission that Acosta is a proxy for unresolved guilt about someone unnamed

open_loops: The children's books retrieved from the collapsed house may contain a working Storywalking method
Boyd's unnamed person he failed to help: who is it?
The Brundles lake is not the Lake of Tears; where is the real one?
Sophia has asked to live with Sara, which Kristi blocked; what is that dynamic building toward?

payoffs.what: The phrase 'Lake of Tears' first surfaces in Ethan's arrival dream (S01E01/E02); here Ethan names it and Jim's ghost confirms it exists in the place

contradiction.wants: To find a way forward, to break the pattern of loss
contradiction.does: Assigns Acosta the task of cataloguing the dead's belongings, which is exactly the act of staying inside the loss rather than escaping it

tone_notes: A 55-second silence at 08:39-09:34 separates the closing of the burial from the opening of Boyd's speechlessness, the longest pause in the episode. Density map shows two conversation-heavy corridors around minutes 31-32 (190 words/min, highest of episode) during the collapsed-house retrieval, and minute 43-44 (134 words/min) when Ethan negotiates with Jade at the Brundles. The low-density trench at minute 21 (5 words) sits exactly at Jade's frustrated meditation, a near-silent beat of blocked memory.
